ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “do you yet understand?” In Chan records it is a recurring public-interview question after the identified master has spoken, displayed an object, stood up, or made another gesture.
EvidenceBody: The addressee may answer “I do not understand”; the identified master may then speak again, request an object, or close the address. In hall discourse it also turns from an exposition to the assembly: “Do you get it? If not yet…” A long pause, a verse, a staff gesture, or the closing “take care” is frequently recorded after the question. The distinctive Chan deployment is therefore not a private report of comprehension but an observable demand made to an emperor, official, monk, or whole assembly in a recorded encounter.
